overall_summary: Analysis of recent YouTube Shorts performance for FACTVERSE reveals a clear dominance in 'What If' space scenarios and extreme planetary extremes. Content focusing on hypotheticals involving weird planets (e.g., diamond planets, burning ice, dark planets) and cosmic curiosities achieve significantly higher views-per-day and engagement (likes/comments-per-view) compared to older psychological tricks or minor animal facts. Recent uploads like Venus's day/year paradox and falling into extreme worlds are pulling top velocity.

winning_patterns.pattern: 'What If You Fell Into...' Space Hypotheses
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views in ~6 days) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views) outperform standard descriptive facts by over 3x.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more high-stakes hypothetical space scenario shorts, focusing on sensory immersion and impossible physics.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (932 views in under 24 hours) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) show exceptional immediate velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Target bizarre planetary mechanics and extreme weather phenomena on newly discovered exoplanets.

weak_patterns.evidence: Shorts like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5-53 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) suffer from low click-through and flat engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological truisms unless framed through an extreme, high-concept narrative or thriller lens.
